newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected steady to up.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called steady to up 0.300 cent, livestock analysts said.

Higher cash hog prices reported early on strong packer demand were expected to spark demand in hog futures. Marketing of hogs backed up by harsh weather last week has finished and hog runs have tightened, especially in areas where farmers are starting fieldwork, analysts said.
Continued underlying support from the Taiwan pork ban was also expected. Demand for U.S. pork is expected to rise in the next couple of months, they said.
Technicians cited a bullish chart configuration following the April contract expiration. The weekly charts point to a much higher price level in hog futures, they said.
Pork belly futures were seen opening higher following the weekly CME Out-of-Town storage report. The report appeared bullish based on the small in-movement last week compared to last year, they said.
CME reported a weekly net in-movement of pork bellies into CME approved warehouses outside Chicago of 353,000 lbs versus 1.99 million lbs in last year.
